1 INTRODUCTION 
This plan is written in accordance with the requirements of IMOs “Guidelines for The 
Development of The Inventory of Hazardous Materials” (Resolution MEPC. 379(80), “Hong 
Kong International Convention for the safe and Environmentally Sound Recycling of Ships, 
2009” (SR/CONF/45) and EU SRR (EU) No 1257/2013. 
The hazardous material survey involved the investigation and identification of hazardous 
materials listed in Table A and Table B of MEPC. 379(80) or Annex I and Annex II of EMSA 
Guidance on IHM. 
The purpose of this plan is to reflect the inventory detailing the type, amount and location of 
hazardous materials used in the vessel construction and operations. 
This report is prepared for developing and providing safe working conditions for the vessel 
crew, protecting the marine environment. 
From the site survey and laboratory analysis results from an ISO 17025 accredited laboratory, 
a register of hazardous materials has been produced, in accordance with the requirements of 
The Guidelines for the Development of the Inventory of Hazardous Materials (MEPC. 
379(80)).

7.1 METHOD OF SURVEY 
The accommodation, stores, machinery space and other locations were categorized into different 
groups based on their functions. For each group and each deck, we have carried out visual 
inspection for all accommodation areas and samples were collected from one accommodation area 
for similar type by removal of covers, enclosures and cavities. Each sample was given an individual 
number with labels to ensure that no duplicate numbers were produced. (Refer Photographs of the 
sample attached in the appendix 3) 
7.2 ONBOARD SURVEY 
The survey targeted the following material categories: 
• Materials in appendix 1 to the convention (ref. /1/), contained in ship’s structure and 
equipment (IHM PART I). Asbestos, Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), Lead and lead 
compounds, Cadmium and cadmium compounds, Polychlorinated naphthalenes (PCNs), 
Brominated Flame Retardant (HBCDD), Perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS), 
Polybrominated biphenyl (PBB), Polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), Hexavalent 
chromium and hexavalent Chromium compounds, Certain shortchain chlorinated paraffins 
(SCCP), Mercury and mercury compounds and Ozone depleting substances (ODSs). We 
covered all the equipment /Machinery and areas containing hazardous material. 
• All equipment /Machinery and areas potentially containing hazardous material were 
covered. 
 
7.3 SAMPLING 
All samples taken onboard during the IHM assessment were sent to a qualified, ISO 17025 
accredited laboratory for testing. The following are the testing methods and standards followed as 
per appendix 9 of MEPC. 379(80) guidelines two additional hazardous materials (PFOS and 
HBCDD) were tested as per regulation (EU) no 1257/2013.all samples were properly marked and 
accompanied with a sampling log number with information about the sample. All sampling 
locations were photographically documented. While taking samples onboard, two photographs are 
taken - one close up view with samples and the other view showing sample & nearby surrounding 
areas. Both sets of photographs are attached in appendix 3. The sample marked stickers are 
available onboard for future traceability & surveyor verifications, if required.

actinolite asbestos, amosite, anthophyllite asbestos, chrysotile, crocidolite, tremolite asbestos 
 
 
SAMPLE PREPARATION: 
Gravimetric Reduction (pretreatment process) of samples, by Ashing, treatment with 2M 
hydrochloric acid and separation of aggregate by flotation or sedimentation. Visually examine 
samples with a low -magnification stereomicroscope in a hood. In a hood, with tweezers remove 
small, representative portions of the sample. After placing a few drops of RI liquid on the slide, put a 
small portion of sample in the liquid. Tease apart with a needle or smash small clumps with the flat 
end of a spatula or probe, producing a uniform thickness or particles so that better estimates of 
projected area percentages can be made. Mix the fibers and particles on the slide so that they are as 
homogeneous as possible. 
 
QUALITATIVE ASSESSMENT: (POLARIZED LIGHT MICROSCOPY (PLM) 
After placing a few drops of RI liquid on the slide, put a small portion of sample in the liquid. Tease 
apart with a needle or smash small clumps with the flat end of a spatula or probe, producing a 
uniform thickness scans the slide to identify any asbestos minerals using the PLM for optical 
properties of morphology, refractive indices, color, pleochroism, birefringence, extinction 
characteristics, sign of elongation, and dispersion staining characteristics. 
 
CONFIRMATION BY SCANNING ELECTRON MICROSCOPE (SEM) 
All non-metals need to be made conductive by covering the sample with a thin layer of conductive 
material. This is done by using a device called a "sputter coater”. Areas ranging from approximately 
1 cm to 5 microns in width is imaged in a scanning mode using conventional SEM techniques 
(magnification ranging from 20X to approximately 30,000X, spatial resolution of 50 to 100 nm).

1. PURPOSE 
The “management procedure to maintain the part I of IHM” is established for the purpose of 
meeting Regulation 5.3 of the Convention and Par. 5.2.2 of the Guidelines by means of properly 
maintaining, during the ship’s operational stage, the part I of IHM developed according to the 
Convention and the Guidelines. 
2. Maintain the Inventory 
The Company designate a person as responsible for maintaining and updating the Inventory 
for the ship and entrust the duty to him on shore. 
The DP establishes and supervises a system in order to ensure that the inventory on board is 
properly updated and maintained. 
3. Management System to Maintain the Inventory 
Request of Hazardous Material Information 
A person who places an order of structure material, machinery and/or equipment to be installed 
on board the ship should identify the objects for the Inventory and request a repair yard or 
suppliers, etc. of those objects for MD/SDoC showing information of Hazardous Materials. 
Review of Collected Information of Hazardous Materials 
A person who receives the deliveries to be on board the ship should ensure that the information 
of Hazardous Materials is properly collected. 
DEVELOPMENT OF REVISION OF THE INVENTORY 
The DP should develop a revision of the Inventory based on the information collected. 
REVIEW OF REVISION AND INSTRUCTION OF UPDATING INVENTORY 
The DP should confirm that the revision of the Inventory is properly developed, should write 
his signature and others, and should instruct the Chief Engineer to update the IHM on board 
with this revision. 
UPDATE OF THE INVENTORY ONBOARD 
The Chief Engineer should ensure the update of the Inventory on board recognizing that the 
Inventory is an essential part of the certificate on IHM. 
UPDATE OF THE INVENTORY ON BOARD 
Chief Engineer should confirm with DP that, for all the items to be delivered on board, revision 
of the Inventory is properly developed. 
Chief Engineer should recognize that the Inventory on board is an essential supplement of the 
Conventional Certificate on IHM and should replace the Inventory with its revision 
immediately after receiving the revision from DP and maintain IHM up to date at all times. 
Chief Engineer should undergo a renewal survey and update the supplement of the Certificate 
and should report it to DP.
